questions.stem: Choose the CORRECTLY spelled word from the options below:
questions.explanation: B is correct. ACCOMMODATION: AC-COM-MO-DA-TION. Two c's (from ad+com) and two m's (from commodity). This is one of the most commonly misspelled words in English. Memory tip: 'ACCOMMODATION has two c's and two m's — it accommodates them all.'

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:
questions.explanation: C is correct — CONSCIENTOUS is misspelled. The correct spelling is CONSCIENTIOUS (CON-SCI-EN-TI-OUS). The word contains 'scienti-' (related to science/conscience) plus '-ous'. The 'i' before 'ous' is commonly dropped in error. All other words are correctly spelled.

B is correct. SUPERSEDE is the only English word ending in '-sede' (not '-cede' like precede, concede, recede). This makes it a perennial spelling trap. Etymology: Latin super (above) + sedere (sit) — to sit above, replace. Memory: 'Super + sede — it SITS above all others.'

B is correct — SEPERATE is misspelled. The correct spelling is SEPARATE. Mnemonic: 'There is A RAT in SEPARATE' (sepaRATE). This is one of the most frequently confused pairs in English. NECESSARY: one Collar, two Socks (1 c, 2 s).

C is correct. PRIVILEGE: PRI-VI-LEGE. Three syllables. The traps: many add a 'd' (PRIVILEDGE) — wrong; the last syllable is '-lege' not '-ledge'. Etymology: Latin privus (private) + lex/legis (law) — a private law or benefit. No 'd' in the word.

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:
questions.explanation: D is correct — LIASON is misspelled. The correct spelling is LIAISON (LI-AI-SON). The word contains two 'i's — a classic error is writing 'LIASON' with only one 'i'. Note: CALENDER (pressing machine) and CALENDAR (date planner) are both correctly spelled as written, so C is not the answer. The unique error here is the missing 'i' in LIAISON.

B is correct. HARASS: HA-RASS — one 'r', two 's'. The most common error is doubling the 'r' (HARRASS). Etymology: from Old French harer (to incite). Memory: 'Don't get stressed — HARASS has one R, two S.' Just like EMBARRASS has two R's and two S's.

C is correct — RECIEVE is misspelled. The correct spelling is RECEIVE. Rule: 'i before e, except after c' — RECEIVE follows the 'after c' exception → 'ei' not 'ie'. Other examples: conceive, perceive, deceive, ceiling. Memory: 'CEI-ling and re-CEI-ve — after C comes E-I, not I-E.'

A is correct. MANAGEABLE retains the silent 'e' from MANAGE because it is needed to preserve the soft 'g' sound (as in 'gem'). Rule: when adding a suffix starting with a vowel (like '-able'), normally drop the silent 'e'. EXCEPTION: if the 'e' is needed to maintain the soft sound of 'c' or 'g', retain it. Compare: MANAGEABLE (soft g preserved), NOTICEABLE (soft c preserved).

questions.stem: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelled word in the group:
questions.explanation: C is correct — OCASSIONALLY is misspelled. The correct spelling is OCCASIONALLY (OC-CA-SION-AL-LY). The errors: only one 'c' instead of two (OC-CA-), and one 's' in '-sion'. Memory: 'OCCASIONALLY has two c's but only one s — like a suit coat with two CC (Casio watch) but one zipper.'

B is correct. INDISPENSABLE: IN-DIS-PEN-SA-BLE. Ends in '-able', not '-ible'. This is a common error. The '-able/-ible' choice: INDISPENSABLE comes from 'dispense' (Latin dispensare); most '-ense'/'-ense' roots take '-able'. Memory: 'INDISPENSABLE — you cannot dispense with the A (in -able).'

C is correct — MISCHIEVIOUS is misspelled. The correct spelling is MISCHIEVOUS (MIS-CHIE-VOUS). There is NO extra 'i' before '-ous'. Many writers hypercorrect it as 'mischievious' by analogy with 'devious' or 'previous', but those words have different roots. The word is: MIS + CHIEV + OUS. Memory: 'MISCHIEVOUS is not devious — no extra i.'
